findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: Sending more than 4 bytes from the client
findings.assumptions: The size of the buffer is assumed to be sizeof(uint32_t) which is 4 bytes. The client can control the data sent to the server.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: Sending a string that includes format specifiers like %x to the server
findings.assumptions: The printf() function is used to display the received data, which could potentially lead to format string vulnerabilities if the data is not properly sanitized.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.trigger: Inputting a number larger than the maximum value of uint32_t
findings.assumptions: The scanf() function is used to read user input, which could potentially lead to integer overflow if the input is not properly validated.

findings.title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
findings.trigger: Sending a large number of messages from the client
findings.assumptions: The server does not have any limits on the number of messages it can handle, which could potentially lead to resource exhaustion.
